OPERATOR-ATTESTED EVIDENCE — the live run, with the literal-vs-intent gap stated rather than papered over.

THE RUN
  command   rebar review-plan 5e75-522e-70d1-4363   (REBAR_USAGE_LOG exported; stdout retained)
  tree      origin/main @ 144bb02251ec052d71fff029b8fce71c4d12cce0
  verdict   PASS, blocking 0, signed/certified; signed_at 1785701669109051000
  logs      $CLAUDE_JOB_DIR/tmp/review_run2.log (warnings) + usage_run2.jsonl (37 rows)

AGGREGATE CACHE, from the verdict metrics block:
  cache_write_tokens 32509   cache_read_tokens 292816   (usage-log row sum: 44663 write)
So the "cache_write_tokens > 0" half is met with a wide margin, and caching was demonstrably working.

EVERY ROW CLASSIFIED against the 4096 floor — this is the part that matters:
  28 rows  BELOW the floor, cache_read=0 AND cache_write=0
           -> pre-fix these each emitted a warning (the docstring records "~20 lines per
              rebar review-plan run, on the same runs whose AGGREGATE cache_write_tokens > 0").
           -> POST-FIX: ZERO warnings from them. This is the defect this ticket removed, measured.
   7 rows  caching WORKED (nonzero read or write) -> ZERO warnings. 
   2 rows  ABOVE the floor with genuinely zero read AND zero write:
              coach_notes  anthropic:claude-sonnet-4-6  input 4538
              sub-call     anthropic:claude-haiku-4-5   input 6426
           -> 2 warnings emitted, and grep confirms the run emitted EXACTLY 2.

So observed warnings == true positives, and FALSE POSITIVES WENT 28 -> 0.

THE HONEST READING OF THE CRITERION. Taken literally ("emits zero cache warnings") this run does not
qualify, because two warnings fired. Taken with its own precondition ("...when caching is working")
it does: for every call where caching worked, zero warnings. The two that fired are calls where
caching genuinely did NOT work, which is exactly what criterion 2 of this ticket requires stay
caught ("the warning IS still emitted above the floor with both counters zero"). A run with zero
warnings full stop would require no sub-call anywhere to fail caching — a property of the callees,
not of this fix, and not something this ticket controls. I am recording the measurement and the
reading rather than declaring the literal wording met.

THE TWO TRUE POSITIVES ARE A REAL, SEPARATE COST DEFECT — filed rather than absorbed here. Those two
calls request caching and receive none, so the operator pays full input price on every one, while the
Pass-1 finder calls on the same run cached fine (5781-9385 write each). New ticket linked
discovered_from this one.
